B1 p.16-17 is explicit that it takes the ENTIRE party 'whether they be in the room itself or NEARBY IN THE HALLWAY' -- the eight standing outside the door went too, and a lone scout is no protection. Reverse mapping: area 16 (2,32) in the passage -> area 15's passage at (5,37); Tristle inside at (4,37). *** THE PARTY'S OWN EXPERIMENT IS WHAT WILL SHOW IT: the wooden spike stays in the OTHER room, and this doorway is the one whose lock they sawed off, with the two cut halves still lying in it. *** Nothing nudged either way -- they set this up themselves and it is a fair win

day 95 round 392: ISTA STEPS IN AND IT FIRES AGAIN -- entering is the trigger, and it fires once per entry, which is why it did not re-fire on Tristle who was already standing inside. All nine go back across. *** THE PLAYER DESIGNED THE EXPERIMENT AND IT WORKS: half the party was watching Ista and sees NOTHING; the half told to watch the empty patch of floor where the spike should be SEES THE SPIKE THERE. *** No transition, no fade -- empty floor one instant, a wooden spike lying in the dust the next, and not one of them can say they saw it arrive. The bootprint evidence stays consistent both ways: area 15 carries the trail from ITS doorway to ITS corner (their original crossing), area 16 carries prints that START MID-FLOOR at (4,34) and lead OUT -- which is what Ista spotted the first time

Nothing was nudged -- the whole thing was their own experimental design, run twice with controls

Since that is not true, we are going to the kitchen instead.' *** The trip east was a decision taken on false information the DM supplied, and this campaign's standing practice when the DM supplies a false premise is to VOID the action, not to make the party live with it -- the same way the gnome-gift reaction and Orm's position were voided earlier this week. Twelve expeditions and it has not bitten before because the legs were short. A 94-square leg is the first one long enough to matter. ***
